technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client integration and configuration conventions for module and xd-admin self-registration.

Implement module state publication as an idempotent registration/update operation, with the module identity and current state represented as Eureka instance metadata or equivalent service-instance data.
Refactor ContainersController, StreamsController, ModulesController, and JobsController to depend on an Admin SPI abstraction rather than deployment-specific implementation calls.
Expose module metrics through Spring Boot Actuator-compatible REST endpoints, with Spring Integration channel-based metrics supported where required by the existing module runtime.
Persist periodic metrics snapshots using the existing Spring Boot metrics export mechanism and Redis as the default storage backend, while keeping the interval configurable.
Port FTP modules by adapting existing Spring XD implementations to the s-c-s module packaging, configuration, and launcher conventions rather than rewriting their core FTP behavior.
Use the repository's existing CI platform for repeatable build and test workflows, and use Docker image build and push steps for the module-launcher image.
Treat automated unit, integration, and workflow validation as part of each feature's implementation rather than as a separate manual-only verification step.
assumptions: The existing s-c-s and Spring XD repositories build successfully or have only minor unrelated baseline issues before this increment begins.
Existing Eureka server, Redis, DockerHub credentials, repository permissions, and CI runners are available; provisioning external infrastructure is out of scope.
The required Eureka client libraries and Spring Boot Actuator dependencies can be used without a major framework upgrade.
The existing module launcher and module contract provide stable extension points for registration, metrics exposure, and FTP module packaging.
No new authentication, authorization, tenancy, or encryption model is required beyond the mechanisms already present in the repositories.
The four controller refactors preserve existing REST behavior and focus on routing operations through the Admin SPI.
Metrics requirements are limited to capturing, exposing, and periodically persisting existing runtime metrics; creation of a new metrics taxonomy or dashboard is out of scope.
CI scope covers build, unit/integration test execution, artifact packaging, and Docker image publication, but not migration to a new CI provider.
DockerHub publication uses an existing springcloud organization or repository naming convention and does not require organizational approval work.
Effort includes implementation, code-level tests, local integration verification, and developer documentation, but excludes elapsed waiting time for external reviews or infrastructure approvals.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the s-c-s and Spring XD module, controller, SPI, Eureka, metrics, build, and CI structures; identify reusable implementations and finalize interfaces, configuration points, and compatibility constraints.

activities.activity_name: Module Eureka state registration and update
activities.activity_description: Implement module-side registration and state update behavior, configuration for Eureka connectivity and instance identity, lifecycle handling, and unit/integration tests verifying registration and updates.
Configure xd-admin as a Eureka client, implement startup registration and status metadata, handle lifecycle and failure behavior, and add tests for discoverability configuration.

Refactor ContainersController, StreamsController, ModulesController, and JobsController to invoke the appropriate Admin SPI implementation while preserving existing REST contracts, deployment selection, error handling, and tests.

activities.activity_name: Direct module metrics capture and REST exposure
activities.activity_description: Implement module-level metrics collection using the available Spring Integration and Spring Boot Actuator mechanisms, expose the resulting metrics through REST APIs, define configuration and response mapping, and add endpoint and runtime tests.

Implement configurable periodic metrics export and persistence using Redis by default, including scheduling, serialization, retention or key conventions consistent with the existing repository, failure handling, and persistence tests.
Port the existing Spring XD FTP source modules into the s-c-s repository, adapt metadata, configuration, packaging, and launcher integration, and verify representative FTP source pipeline behavior.

Create or update CI configuration to compile s-c-s components, execute unit and applicable integration tests, publish build artifacts as needed, and document required build variables and workflow behavior.

Add CI steps to build and bundle the module-launcher image, apply repository and version tags, authenticate securely to DockerHub, publish the image, and validate the workflow with a representative build.

Run end-to-end verification across Eureka discovery, Admin SPI controller operations, module metrics REST access and Redis persistence, FTP module execution, CI artifacts, and Docker image consumption; fix integration defects.

Document configuration, endpoint usage, metrics persistence, Eureka registration, FTP module usage, CI secrets, and Docker image tagging; perform code cleanup and prepare the increment for review and release.
